passage: By the second period on Thursday, Pablo knew that half the class had heard about his failed orchestra audition. He had told only Alejandro. His first plan was a furious message listing everything Alejandro had done wrong since primary school. He typed two lines, deleted them and put the phone in his bag. That night at the kitchen table in Valencia, he took a sheet of paper and drew a line down the middle. What hurt: hearing it from Marta first. Feeling laughed at. What I want: for Alejandro to know it hurt, and to be someone I can tell things to again. Pablo read the second column twice. It had never been about winning the argument. On Friday he would ask Alejandro to walk home with him.

qa.q: How many lines did Pablo type before deleting the message?
qa.a: Pablo typed two lines and deleted them.

qa.q: How did Pablo feel about Alejandro telling the class, and where can you tell?
qa.a: Pablo felt hurt and laughed at; the page lists hearing it from Marta first and feeling laughed at.

qa.q: What approach could Pablo take on Friday, and why might it work?
qa.a: Pablo could ask to talk privately and begin with 'I felt hurt when...', because that invites Alejandro to listen without feeling attacked.

qa.q: How might Alejandro see the news spreading?
qa.a: Alejandro may not realise how much it hurt, and could feel defensive if blamed, so a calm private request gives Alejandro a chance to listen and repair trust.

grounding: After a friend shares a secret with others, the student waits a night, writes what hurt and what he wants, and realises the goal is to be heard and trusted again, not to win.

passage: At the boarding school in Mussoorie, news travelled fast. By dinner on Tuesday, half the dorm was humming the choir song at Tenzin, and he knew Uday had told them about his crush. Uday was the only one he had told. Tenzin's face burned. He wanted to walk over to Uday's table and say something cruel enough to get even. Instead he went to the study hall after dinner, took out a sheet and wrote two headings. What hurt: not the teasing. That it was Uday. What I want: he stared at the second heading a long time. To make Uday feel bad? For a minute, yes. Then, underneath: for Uday to understand. To be able to trust him again. He folded the page into his pocket and decided to sleep on it before saying anything.

qa.q: What was the dorm humming at Tenzin?
What was Tenzin feeling at dinner?
qa.a: He felt humiliated and betrayed, his face burning, and angry enough to want to get even.

qa.q: What could Tenzin say to Uday the next day, given what he wrote?
qa.a: Talk privately, say it hurt most because it was Uday, and ask why it happened, since the goal is to be understood and trusted again, not to win.

qa.q: How might Uday feel when Tenzin doesn't confront him at dinner?
qa.a: Uday may feel uneasy or guilty, sensing something is wrong, and perhaps relieved there was no scene.

grounding: Shows a student, after a friend spreads a secret, waiting a night and writing down what hurt and what he really wants.

passage:
Anjali,
I wanted to shout at you yesterday, so I waited. I'm writing this the next morning instead. You told Priyank and the others that I cried in the library after the Maths mock. I told only you. What hurt wasn't that they laughed. It was that you were the one I trusted, and it felt like that didn't count. Last night I wrote a list of what I want now. At first it said "for you to feel as bad as I did". I crossed that out. What I actually want is for you to understand why it mattered, and for us to get back to a place where I can tell you things. I'm not trying to win anything. Can we talk after school on Thursday?
Sachin

qa.a: Sachin felt angry and betrayed, wanting to shout, because the one trusted person had shared something private.

qa.q: Why is waiting a night before responding a wise choice here?
qa.a: It gave Sachin time to see the real goal, being understood and trusted again, instead of saying something hurtful that would make repair harder.

qa.q: How might Anjali feel reading the letter?
qa.a: Anjali may feel ashamed and sorry, seeing how much the trust meant, and relieved to be offered a talk rather than a fight 🤍.

grounding: A student's letter, written after waiting a night, names what hurt and realises the goal is to be heard and trusted again, not to win.
